For a typical household fridge, you need a power station with a surge rating of at least 1,200W and about 1,000Wh of capacity. That covers most of a day. These figures come from HomeGridHQ's guide, which uses manufacturer and Department of Energy typical ratings. I couldn't read the Anker and powerstations.reviews pages because they were too large to load, so the numbers below come from the HomeGridHQ page only. ([source](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))

**Two numbers to check**
1. **Surge or start power.** The compressor briefly pulls about 900–1,200W when it kicks on. Look for an inverter that handles at least 1,200W. Many units under 500Wh have inverters that are too small for this, so a 300Wh power bank usually won't work.
2. **Capacity (Wh).** A fridge draws about 100–200W while the compressor runs, but it cycles on and off. HomeGridHQ assumes about 150W running at a 35% duty cycle. That works out to roughly 62Wh per hour with the door kept closed.

**Typical running and start watts**
- Mini fridge: 80W running, 600W start
- Top-freezer, 18 cu ft: 120W running, 1,000W start
- French door, 25 cu ft: 180W running, 1,200W start
- Chest freezer: 100W running, 800W start

**Estimated runtime by capacity**
- About 1,000Wh: about 16 hours
- About 2,000Wh: about 32 hours
- 4,000Wh or more: 2.5 days or more

These are the guide's estimates. Real runtime depends on your fridge, the room temperature, and how often the door is opened.

**Options from that guide** (prices are as listed there and may have changed)
- About 1,000Wh, for outages up to a day:
  - [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D7PPG25F?tag=homegridhq-20), $499, about 17 hours
  - [Anker SOLIX C1000](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C5C89QKZ?tag=homegridhq-20), $470, about 17 hours
  - [OUPES Mega 1](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DG8JQNS4?tag=homegridhq-20), $469, about 17 hours
- About 2,000Wh, for roughly a day and a third:
  - [Jackery Explorer 2000 v2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DFG2WDQH?tag=homegridhq-20), $899, about 33 hours
  - [Bluetti AC200L](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac200l), $899, about 33 hours
- 3,000Wh or more, for multi-day outages:
  - [Bluetti Elite 300](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/elite-300-portable-power-station), $1,199, about 2 days
  - [EcoFlow Delta Pro 3](https://us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-pro-3-portable-power-station), $2,799, about 2.8 days

**Tips**
- Keep the fridge and freezer doors closed as much as possible.
- USDA guidance says food in a closed fridge is unsafe after about 4 hours without power. A full, closed freezer holds for roughly 24–48 hours.
- For a longer outage, add solar panels to recharge the station, or pick a bigger battery.
- If you also want to run lights, a router, or a CPAP, add their wattage and hours to the total.

If you tell me your fridge's size or its nameplate wattage, and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one or two picks.

 What Size Power Station Do You Need to Run a Refrigerator?
 Verified October 2026  Manufacturer + DOE typical ratings. [Methodology](/about/)
 Quick answer: To run a refrigerator you need a power station with at least 1,200W of surge (to start the compressor) and about 1,000Wh of capacity to cover most of a day. A modern full-size fridge uses 100-200 watts while the compressor runs , surges to 900-1,200 watts at compressor start, and averages 30-50W over a day thanks to cycling. For backup sizing, plan around 150W running, 1,200W surge, and a ~35% duty cycle. 
 Refrigerator wattage by type
 Type Running watts Compressor start 
 Mini fridge 80W 600W 
 Top-freezer 18 cu ft 120W 1,000W 
 French door 25 cu ft 180W 1,200W 
 Garage chest freezer 100W 800W 
 Refrigerators are the most common reason to buy backup power - a fridge holds $200-400 of food, and the USDA says food is unsafe after 4 hours above 40°F with the door closed. The good news: fridges are cheap to back up. At a 35% duty cycle, one uses only ~62Wh per hour after inverter losses. Keep the door shut and even a 1kWh station protects your food most of a day. The number that disqualifies small inverters is the compressor start surge - clear 1,200W and you're safe.
 How long real power stations run a refrigerator
 Computed from each unit's rated capacity at 85% inverter efficiency and a 35% duty cycle (150W running, 1,200W start). Units whose continuous output can't run it, whose motor-start surge can't start it are excluded. Where a maker's headline surge only applies to resistive loads, we size starts off continuous output.
